entries.description: Reviewed the completed template-encoding handoff, the Phase 2 roadmap, binding planning notes, and all remaining Phase 2 session-set specs through routed analysis, then created docs/planning/accessibility-and-stubbing-review-ledger.md to freeze the validated baseline and Session 1 decisions.

Confirmed the retained supported surface, accepted app baseline, and accessibility requirements still match this set's assumptions. No core rebaseline was needed beyond documenting the narrow stubbed-uat overlap and freezing the execution notes in the new ledger.

Used routed analysis to re-scan cross-set and intra-set overlap, then updated docs/session-sets/accessibility-and-stubbing/spec.md and docs/session-sets/stubbed-uat/spec.md so the only safe early overlap is explicit: stubbed-uat Sessions 1-2 may begin after accessibility-and-stubbing Session 3 freezes the shared stub abstractions, while later work stays blocked.

Used routed analysis plus the current reusable-surface test-home inventory to freeze the initial components, reports, security-adjacent UI, and WCAG evidence targets in docs/planning/accessibility-and-stubbing-review-ledger.md, including the need for dedicated ParameterPromptForm and ReportViewer proof.

Ran dotnet build Dabbler.Platform.sln and dotnet test Dabbler.Platform.sln --no-build sequentially. Build succeeded with the repo's existing 11 CS1591 XML-doc warnings in src/Libs/Dabbler.Security/Services/DevEmailInbox.cs, and all 370 tests passed across the seven test projects.

Sent the Session 1 spec context, the new review ledger, the downstream stubbed-uat spec update, the activity-log entries, and the sequential build/test evidence to external session verification and saved the raw review output. The verifier returned VERIFIED with no blocking issues.
